fact.description: One short line, e.g. 'Vegetarian; allergic to peanuts.'

name: remember_about_user

name: remember_memory

description: Ask the user to approve a consequential action before you do it: sending a message or email, posting or publishing, buying or paying, deleting data, changing account settings or permissions. action.description: What you want to do, as a short imperative, e.g. 'Send the reply to Dana'.

details.description: Exactly what will happen, including the full text you'll send.

Never ask for secrets in chat. Waits up to 10 minutes for them to hand control back, and returns their note. If it returns pending, end your turn; you'll get a message when they hand back.

instructions.description: Markdown: the purpose, the inputs it needs, where to get information, the steps, checks before finishing, the output format, and what to do when something fails.

quiet.description: For checks that often find nothing (a daily look for renewals, a weekly inbox sweep): runs with nothing worth telling end with 'Nothing to report.' and don't notify the user.

name: update_task

description: Type one field of a saved login or card into the field that has keyboard focus on your screen: click the field first. You never see the value. A login only fills on its own site; a card needs an approved purchase (start_purchase). Take a screenshot afterwards to check.

field.description: Logins: username or password. Cards: number, expiry (MM/YY), cvc, name, zip.

name: vault_fill

description: List the logins and payment cards the user saved in the vault for you, and your spending budget. You never see the secrets themselves: vault_fill types them for you.
name: vault_list

description: Wake yourself or a specified teammate (bot_id) a set time before events on the user's Google Calendar (their primary calendar). Each event starts a run in that teammate's Scheduled chat with the event, once per occurrence, and again if it moves. Cancelled, all-day and declined events don't count. The teammate must have Google Calendar. Use it for things like 'brief me 30 minutes before meetings with guests'.

account.description: With several Google Calendar accounts: the address to watch.

bot_id.description: A teammate's id from list_bots. Where optional, leave it out for yourself. Changing another teammate's setup may ask the user first.

events.description: guests: only events with other people on them.

lead_minutes.description: How many minutes before each event to wake up. 0 is when it starts.

prompt.description: What to do before each event. You'll get this with the event.

name: watch_calendar

description: Wake yourself or a specified teammate (bot_id) when new mail arrives in the user's Gmail. Mail matching the search starts a run in that teammate's Scheduled chat with the new messages, checked every 2 minutes; mail the user sends doesn't count. The teammate must have Gmail. Use it for things like 'tell me when the school writes' or 'file every receipt'.

account.description: With several Gmail accounts: the address to watch.

bot_id.description: A teammate's id from list_bots. Where optional, leave it out for yourself. Changing another teammate's setup may ask the user first.

prompt.description: What to do with the new mail. You'll get this with the messages.

query.description: A Gmail search the new mail must match, like 'from:school.org' or 'subject:invoice has:attachment'. Leave it out for all new mail.

name: watch_gmail

description: Watch a web page for yourself or a specified teammate (bot_id). Changes start a run in that teammate's Scheduled chat, for example for prices, stock, job boards or status pages. Checks run without a browser session and only see what a signed-out visitor sees. The first check just learns the page.

bot_id.description: A teammate's id from list_bots. Where optional, leave it out for yourself. Changing another teammate's setup may ask the user first.

look_for.description: Optional text to wait for, e.g. 'In stock'. Then it fires only when the text appears, not on every change.

prompt.description: What you should do when it changes. You'll get this with the lines that changed.

url.description: The page's absolute http or https URL.

name: watch_page
